title: Jagged Indian Paneer Rasmalai
description: Sweet and creamy Indian rasmalai dessert featuring paneer, red chilli flakes, and a tagine-cooked twist. Perfect for a keto-friendly brunch or dessert.

ingredients.name: Paneer (Indian Cheese)
ingredients.notes: High-quality cheese is essential for a great rasmalai.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.notes: Whole milk is recommended for the best flavor and texture.

ingredients.name: Red Onion
ingredients.notes: Red onion adds a sweet and crunchy texture to the dish.

ingredients.name: Fresh Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Fresh cilantro adds a fresh and herbaceous flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Red Chilli Flakes
ingredients.notes: The heat from the red chilli flakes balances the sweetness of the milk.

ingredients.name: Ghee or Clarified Butter
ingredients.notes: Ghee adds a rich and creamy flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Cardamom Powder
ingredients.notes: Cardamom powder adds a unique and aromatic flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Sugar balances the heat from the red chilli flakes.

instructions: Combine paneer, milk, red onion, and cilantro in a blender and blend until smooth.
Strain the mixture into a bowl and add red chilli flakes, ghee, and cardamom powder.
Heat the mixture in a tagine or a large saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly.
Simmer the mixture for 10-15 minutes or until it thickens slightly.
Remove from heat and let it cool to room temperature.
Chill the rasmalai in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve the rasmalai cold, garnished with fresh cilantro and a drizzle of honey if desired.
